label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Revision-authored AQA-style practice. Orchard Outdoors has a large stock of last season's jackets. It is profitable on paper but cash is tied up in inventory and supplier invoices fall due next month.
question.stem: Which action and trade-off best address Orchard Outdoors' immediate cash-flow problem?

options.label: A
options.text: Buy more jackets on credit; this must improve liquidity because inventory is an asset.

options.label: B
options.text: Offer a carefully priced clearance promotion to convert slow-moving stock into cash, recognising that lower margins could reduce profit.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase depreciation in the accounts; this creates cash in the bank immediately.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase recorded sales revenue without collecting customer payments; this is equivalent to cash received.

option_rationale: A is incorrect because extra inventory can increase working-capital pressure even if a purchase is on credit.
B is correct because selling slow-moving inventory for cash may help liquidity, but discounting can lower margins and profitability.
C is incorrect because depreciation is normally a non-cash accounting charge, not an inflow.
D is incorrect because recognised credit sales do not equal bank receipts.
mark_scheme.model_answer: B. Clearance can release cash from inventory, but a reduced selling price may lower contribution; management should balance liquidity and profitability.
